# the contributor audit: planar frustum dual and collective reflected slabs

## Planar affine frustum

Source: `candidate d28e829ed5b07592`.

The physical layer records agree at s=1 and have their unique nonzero moment root s*=1/(1-2alpha) when alpha<1/2. The other branches have one strict moment sign, so only horizontal and infinity records can occur in a centered law. The bounded-slope replacement retains P,C,M, including the tail atom.

The proposed kappa makes kappa-t=beta(1-t) and kappa(1+e*)=v*+t. Thus the lower and upper corrected inequalities are exactly the two inequalities stated in the proof. The lower inequality needs no centering: when e<1 its quotient R is decreasing, and the endpoint polynomial in b=1-2alpha, x=bT-1 has nonnegative coefficients and a positive denominator. The upper inequality is a true moment dual, not a reduction to individually centered layers.

I independently checked, by symbolic expansion, the R derivative, the R(T)-kappa factorization, the middle-regime squared factor, and all42 entries of the two Bernstein tables in the small-s regime. All identities are exact. The signs of their denominators are positive throughout 0<alpha<1/2. The cubic Bernstein certificates are correct. Averaging removes precisely the moment multiplier, so atoms and arbitrary probability laws on the compact interval are allowed.

The beta comparison and beta<=1/2 are correct; therefore the infinity record is retained. The proof establishes the claimed 4/9 lower bound for the complete planar affine-frustum class in its stated normalization. A constant axial profile and an increasing affine profile need their own trivial/reflected treatment if the wording is expanded to all affine functions. No changing-slope or higher-dimensional dual is inferred.

## Reflected outer pairs

Source: `candidate ce44858a93e72add`.

For two identical central fibers B at0,1, concavity of every support roof forces each exterior fiber to lie in B. At the centroid mark(0,0), a cap written u.x>=tz receives the ordinary Gamma_d payment from B. If t<=0 every reflected outer pair covers one full A_k. If t>0, its missing part reflects into B in the open band kt<u.x<(k+1)t. These bands are disjoint over k and are all paid by the same other-central cap. This proves the exact collective lower bound Gamma_d|B|+sum|A_k|. Pure base caps are separately sufficient and retain boundary mass.

For a single reflected pair and B=-B, large opposite continuous-normal caps at both middle sources give a global cover with common mass |B|/2+|A|, matching the all-normal lower bound. The homothetic contraction A_t within A and its reflected partner retain actual canonical fibers, with no enlargement of B. The exact ratio decreases to1/4. Independent contraction of many outer pairs is deliberately not asserted.

The theorem uses d>=1 and d-dimensional volume, with full-dimensional B. It is not an intrinsic-degeneracy reduction for the main task. It also retains the condition that the reflection center is the centroid of B. Subject to those explicit scopes, analytic audit PASS.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
